78840.subject: Crypto Still Loves Memecoins -Just Not Hunter Biden's
78840.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Hunter Biden's LAPTOP](https://thedefiant.io/news/tokens/hunter-biden-laptop-falls-99-percent-three-hours-trump-valuation)**[ fell 99% in three hours to TRUMP's valuation](https://thedefiant.io/news/tokens/hunter-biden-laptop-falls-99-percent-three-hours-trump-valuation)

* **[Pump.fun](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-lets-creators-launch-coins-priced-in-tokenized-stocks)**[ now lets creators price new coins in tokenized stocks](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-lets-creators-launch-coins-priced-in-tokenized-stocks)

* **[Consensys](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/consensys-software-inc-splits-in-two-rebrands-as-metamask)**[ is splitting in two and renaming itself MetaMask](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/consensys-software-inc-splits-in-two-rebrands-as-metamask)

* **[Bitcoin](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-gives-back-overnight-gain-brent-tops-100-sep-9-2026)**[ gave back its overnight gain as Brent cleared $100](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-gives-back-overnight-gain-brent-tops-100-sep-9-2026)

* **[Circle](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/circle-to-acquire-tazapay-in-400-million-all-stock-payments-deal)**[ is buying Singapore's Tazapay for $400 million in stock](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/circle-to-acquire-tazapay-in-400-million-all-stock-payments-deal)

* **[Oasis Vault](https://www.oasisvault.io/cryptopunk)**[ is giving away CryptoPunk 909 (Partner)](https://www.oasisvault.io/cryptopunk)

Hunter Biden's LAPTOP opened at $247.55 and traded at $1.90 three hours later. It is now CoinGecko's worst 24-hour performer, ahead of every other token on the site.

Buyers got thin pools and team supply on the other side. The Aerodrome and Uniswap V4 books opened nearly empty, and an address Arkham tags as Wintermute [sold 466,255 tokens for about $2.08 million after receiving part of a 2.5 million-token team allocation](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/report-links-2-08m-in-laptop-sales-to-wintermute-tagged-wallet). The claim page asks for an email address rather than a wallet signature. Biden's own launch post told readers not to expect him to make the token more valuable for them, and 3.4 million people read it.

The format is doing fine. Robinhood Chain has run on memecoins quoted in tokenized equities since July, and on Wednesday afternoon[ Pump.fun opened the same trade](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-lets-creators-launch-coins-priced-in-tokenized-stocks) on Solana with 93 quote pairs, including tokenized Nvidia, Tesla and the S&P 500, and half the fees routed into buying PUMP. What crypto turned down was another celebrity blatantly trying to profit off the space.

Caption: 

“If I stop practice for one day, I notice it in my playing; if I stop two days, my friends notice it; if I stop three days, the public notices it.”
_— __Hans von Bülow__ _



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/de8d3560-751e-45e3-8f25-017bcb18c9b7/unnamed.jpg?t=1788987364)
Caption: 

# AI could make markets unintelligible

Once a year, a few of us from the investment bank I worked at in the aughts would trek from our office tower in gleaming Canary Wharf to the uncharted wilderness of South London.

There, we’d hope not to be mugged before getting to a nondescript building that our employee-ID cards mysteriously gave us access to. We’d take an unmarked elevator to the second floor, because that’s where we were told to go.

The creaking door would open directly onto a trading floor — a near replica of the one in Canary Wharf.

But dingy and windowless. With computers that were at least a decade old: bulky, deep-backed monitors in beige casing attached to CPU towers that still had slots for CD-ROMs and floppy disks. 

We were there to check that our modern trading systems worked on this archaic equipment. 

Miraculously, they did. We could execute and book our trades just like we did in Canary Wharf. Slowly, because the square monitors only had room for one application at a time. But surely.

Everything worked.

This was our “contingency site,” maintained year-round by the IT staff. And the cleaning staff, too, who can’t have had much to do besides dust, because no one ever used it.

It must have cost the bank a fortune. But it was an important insurance policy — and not just for the bank. 

In case of emergency —  earthquake, cyberattack, Godzilla — every investment bank in London had a contingency trading floor to fall back on. Markets would continue to function, no matter what.

Today’s markets may need a similar insurance policy, but on a much larger scale.

In case of an _AI_ emergency, economist Markus K. Brunnermeier believes we should have a contingency option for the entire financial system — a market that works the way markets did at least a decade ago.

**Trading like it’s 1999**

Bill Gates thinks policymakers should reserve parts of the economy for humans: “I believe that as AI and robots improve,” he recently [wrote](https://www.gatesnotes.com/work/make-ai-work-for-everyone/reader/
